title: Scientists use “empty space” to strengthen superconductivity
summary:
Researchers have shown that tiny quantum fluctuations in a vacuum can strengthen superconductivity. Their study describes a new way to control how certain materials behave. The source report, published on October 3, 2026, says this is the first experimental demonstration of the effect.

A superconductor is a material that can carry electric current without electrical resistance under certain conditions. Its critical temperature is the temperature below which it becomes superconducting. Raising this temperature means the material can stay superconducting in slightly warmer conditions.

The study, published in Nature, was led by Changgan Zeng and Guanghui Cheng at the University of Science and Technology of China. Researchers from Shanghai Jiao Tong University, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology and other collaborators also took part.

The experiment explored a surprising idea: empty space is not completely still. In quantum physics, even a vacuum in its lowest energy state has tiny fluctuations. Scientists have already observed effects of these fluctuations in other experiments.

Zeng explained that vacuum fluctuations in ordinary free space are generally too weak to produce visible effects in large systems of materials. To strengthen their influence, the team used a specially designed structure called a terahertz dark cavity. It reshapes the electromagnetic environment around a material.

The researchers placed a superconducting material called NbSe2 inside this cavity. They then compared its superconducting behavior inside and outside the structure.

In a device with six layers of NbSe2, the critical temperature increased by up to 5.4%. Cheng reported that the critical current and critical magnetic field also increased significantly near the superconducting transition. These describe limits on the current and magnetic field the material can handle while remaining superconducting.

The team changed several parts of the setup to check other possible explanations. These checks allowed them to rule out effects such as strain, damage to the material and certain influences from nearby metal.

Another clue came from the cavity’s frequency. The improvement reached a peak at a particular frequency instead of changing smoothly. Zeng said this provided strong experimental evidence that the superconducting state was interacting with the cavity’s electromagnetic modes. The findings open a new path for studying and controlling unusual states of matter.
why_it_matters: The findings describe a new way to control material behavior by changing its electromagnetic environment. The experiment strengthened superconductivity and opened a path for studying unusual states of matter.

keywords.explanation: The ability of a material to carry electric current without electrical resistance under certain conditions.
The temperature below which a material becomes superconducting.
Tiny quantum fluctuations present even in a vacuum’s lowest energy state.
A specially designed structure that reshapes the electromagnetic environment around a material.
A limit on the magnetic field a material can handle while remaining superconducting.
Patterns of electromagnetic activity in the cavity that the superconducting state was interacting with, according to Zeng’s interpretation of the evidence.

questions.question: What does the source report published on October 3, 2026, say about the study?
options: It shows that empty space has no activity
It proves every material can become superconducting
It is the first discovery of any vacuum fluctuation
It is the first experimental demonstration of this effect
questions.correct_answer: It is the first experimental demonstration of this effect

questions.question: Where was the study published?
options: In Nature
In the source report only
At Shanghai Jiao Tong University
At the Massachusetts Institute of Technology

questions.question: According to Zeng, why did the team use a specially designed cavity?
options: To damage the NbSe2 before measuring it
To remove the material’s electromagnetic surroundings
To prevent any comparison with conditions outside the cavity
To strengthen the influence of ordinarily weak vacuum fluctuations
questions.correct_answer: To strengthen the influence of ordinarily weak vacuum fluctuations

questions.question: Which result was reported for the device with six layers of NbSe2?
options: Its critical temperature fell by 5.4%
Its critical temperature increased by up to 5.4%
Its number of layers increased by 5.4%
Its electrical resistance increased by up to 5.4%
questions.correct_answer: Its critical temperature increased by up to 5.4%

questions.question: Which possible explanations did the experimental checks rule out?
options: All changes in critical current and critical magnetic field
The existence of vacuum fluctuations
Every possible influence from the electromagnetic environment
Strain, material damage and certain influences from nearby metal
questions.correct_answer: Strain, material damage and certain influences from nearby metal

questions.question: What did Zeng say the peak at a particular cavity frequency supported?
options: The claim that frequency had no effect
The claim that the improvement changed smoothly
The claim that nearby metal damaged the material
Interaction between the superconducting state and the cavity’s electromagnetic modes
questions.correct_answer: Interaction between the superconducting state and the cavity’s electromagnetic modes

perspectives.description: Zeng explained that ordinary free-space vacuum fluctuations are generally too weak to produce visible effects in large material systems. He interpreted the frequency peak as strong evidence of interaction with the cavity’s electromagnetic modes.
Cheng reported significant increases in critical current and critical magnetic field near the superconducting transition.
